# Copyright (c) 2026, Han Guo, Tri Dao.
"""Rotary-position resources and ready-to-use RoPE GEMM epilogues."""

from __future__ import annotations

import cutlass
import cutlass.cute as cute
from cutlass import Boolean, const_expr

import quack.copy_utils as copy_utils
from quack.epilogue.ops import ColVecLoad, EpiOp, RowVecLoad, TileLoad
from quack.epilogue.frontend import gemm_epilogue, pack, unpack


class RotaryCosSinLoad(EpiOp):
    """Per-subtile gmem->rmem load of the interleaved rotary cos/sin table.

    The param tensor is (seqlen_ro, head_dim), row-major, cos at even columns
    and sin at odd columns. Output column n reads table column n % head_dim of
    table row m: the head broadcast is expressed as a stride-0 repeat mode in
    the per-tile gmem view, so a single ``partition_for_epilogue`` makes the
    loaded fragment elementwise-aligned with tRS_rD.

    Requires tile_N % head_dim == 0 or head_dim % tile_N == 0 (the repeat /
    slice views below are built with static layout algebra; a tile that
    straddles a head boundary at a non-multiple offset would need a per-element
    mod). Rows beyond the M limit are left at 0 — those lanes never reach gmem
    (the D store is bound-checked) but must not fault.
    """

    def param_fields(self):
        return [(self.name, object, None)]

    def to_params(self, gemm, args):
        # Stronger than assume_stride_divisibility (32 bits): assume 16-byte
        # stride divisibility so gmem loads can vectorize to 128 bits. The host
        # asserts head_dim (== the row stride of a contiguous table) allows it.
        tensor = getattr(args, self.name)
        divby = 128 // tensor.element_type.width
        new_stride = tuple(
            cute.assume(s, divby=divby) if not cute.is_static(s) else s for s in tensor.stride
        )
        return {
            self.name: cute.make_tensor(
                tensor.iterator, cute.make_layout(tensor.shape, stride=new_stride)
            )
        }

    @cute.jit
    def begin(self, gemm, param, smem_tensor, ctx):
        head_dim = const_expr(param.shape[1])
        tile_M, tile_N = ctx.tile_M, ctx.tile_N
        assert tile_N % head_dim == 0 or head_dim % tile_N == 0, (
            "rotary epilogue requires tile_N to be a multiple or a divisor of head_dim"
        )
        m_tile = ctx.tile_coord_mnkl[0]
        mCS = param
        if const_expr(ctx.varlen_manager.varlen_m):
            mCS = cute.domain_offset(
                (ctx.varlen_manager.params.cu_seqlens_m[ctx.batch_idx], 0), mCS
            )
        if const_expr(tile_N % head_dim == 0):
            # One tile covers >= 1 whole head: repeat the head_dim columns via a
            # stride-0 mode. The view is identical for every N tile coordinate.
            gCS_rows = cute.local_tile(mCS, (tile_M, head_dim), (m_tile, 0))
            gCS = cute.make_tensor(
                gCS_rows.iterator,
                cute.make_layout(
                    (tile_M, (head_dim, tile_N // head_dim)),
                    stride=(gCS_rows.stride[0], (gCS_rows.stride[1], 0)),
                ),
            )
        else:
            # A head spans several tiles: slice the head's columns for this tile.
            gCS = cute.local_tile(
                mCS,
                (tile_M, tile_N),
                (m_tile, ctx.tile_coord_mnkl[1] % (head_dim // tile_N)),
            )
        tDgCS = ctx.partition_for_epilogue_fn(gCS)
        tDcCS = ctx.partition_for_epilogue_fn(cute.make_identity_tensor((tile_M, tile_N)))
        if const_expr(ctx.tiled_copy_t2r is not None):
            tDgCS = ctx.tiled_copy_r2s.retile(tDgCS)
            tDcCS = ctx.tiled_copy_r2s.retile(tDcCS)
        tDgCS = cute.group_modes(tDgCS, 3, cute.rank(tDgCS))
        tDcCS = cute.group_modes(tDcCS, 3, cute.rank(tDcCS))
        limit_m = min(ctx.varlen_manager.len_m(ctx.batch_idx) - m_tile * tile_M, tile_M)
        full_tile = Boolean(limit_m >= tile_M)
        # Subtile iteration count decides the prefetch depth below.
        num_subtiles_static = const_expr(
            cute.size(
                cute.zipped_divide(
                    cute.make_layout(gemm.cta_tile_shape_mnk[:2]), ctx.epi_tile
                ).shape[1]
            )
        )
        # Two per-subtile fragments (double buffer): subtile i+1's loads are
        # issued in begin_loop(i) so their latency hides behind subtile i's
        # rotation + store. With a single subtile per tile (QK-norm's wide epi
        # tiles), skip the second buffer — it would only add register pressure.
        # Layout-matched to the gmem partition; integer indexing is
        # coordinate-order, so they still line up elementwise with tRS_rD.
        # Rows beyond limit_m keep the initial 0.
        buf0 = cute.make_rmem_tensor_like(tDgCS[None, None, None, 0])
        buf0.fill(0.0)
        if const_expr(num_subtiles_static > 1):
            buf1 = cute.make_rmem_tensor_like(tDgCS[None, None, None, 0])
            buf1.fill(0.0)
        else:
            buf1 = buf0
        bufs = [buf0, buf1]
        # Explicit vector width for the gmem->rmem copy: autovec is too
        # conservative for gmem sources, so we build the copy atom ourselves.
        src0_f = cute.coalesce(cute.filter_zeros(tDgCS[None, None, None, 0]))
        dst0_f = cute.coalesce(cute.filter_zeros(bufs[0]))
        copy_vec = const_expr(
            min(cute.max_common_vector(src0_f, dst0_f), 128 // param.element_type.width)
        )
        assert head_dim % copy_vec == 0, "head_dim must be a multiple of the copy vector"
        # Subtile iteration order, to know which epi_coord comes next. Must
        # match the epi_tile_layout built in GemmBase.epilogue.
        epi_tile_shape = cute.zipped_divide(
            cute.make_layout(gemm.cta_tile_shape_mnk[:2]), ctx.epi_tile
        ).shape[1]
        epi_tile_layout = cute.make_ordered_layout(
            epi_tile_shape, order=(0, 1) if const_expr(gemm.epi_m_major) else (1, 0)
        )
        if const_expr(param.element_type != gemm.acc_dtype):
            tDrCS_cvt = cute.make_rmem_tensor(bufs[0].shape, gemm.acc_dtype)
        else:
            tDrCS_cvt = None
        state = [tDgCS, tDcCS, full_tile, limit_m, bufs, tDrCS_cvt, copy_vec, epi_tile_layout]
        # Preload subtile 0 so begin_loop(0) finds it ready.
        self._load_subtile(state, epi_tile_layout.get_hier_coord(0), 0)
        return state

    @cute.jit
    def _load_subtile(self, state, epi_coord, buf_idx: cutlass.Constexpr[int]):
        tDgCS, tDcCS, full_tile, limit_m, bufs, _, copy_vec, _ = state
        tDgCS_cur = tDgCS[None, None, None, epi_coord]
        buf = bufs[buf_idx]
        if full_tile:
            tiler = cute.make_layout(copy_vec)
            copy_atom = copy_utils.get_copy_atom(buf.element_type, copy_vec)
            cute.copy(
                copy_atom,
                cute.zipped_divide(cute.coalesce(cute.filter_zeros(tDgCS_cur)), tiler),
                cute.zipped_divide(cute.coalesce(cute.filter_zeros(buf)), tiler),
            )
        else:
            # Ragged last M tile: per-element row-predicated loads. Slow but
            # only ever runs on the boundary tile.
            tDcCS_cur = tDcCS[None, None, None, epi_coord]
            for i in cutlass.range(cute.size(buf), unroll_full=True):
                if tDcCS_cur[i][0] < limit_m:
                    buf[i] = tDgCS_cur[i]

    @cute.jit
    def begin_loop(self, gemm, state, epi_coord):
        bufs, tDrCS_cvt, epi_tile_layout = state[4], state[5], state[7]
        idx = const_expr(cute.crd2idx(epi_coord, epi_tile_layout))
        num_subtiles = const_expr(cute.size(epi_tile_layout))
        if const_expr(idx + 1 < num_subtiles):
            self._load_subtile(state, epi_tile_layout.get_hier_coord(idx + 1), (idx + 1) % 2)
        cur = bufs[idx % 2]
        if const_expr(tDrCS_cvt is not None):
            tDrCS_cvt.store(cur.load().to(tDrCS_cvt.element_type))
            return tDrCS_cvt
        return cur


class RotaryCosSinLoadHost(RotaryCosSinLoad):
    """The epirope op + the generic host-layer schema hooks it predates."""

    fn_port = "value"

    def host_arg_key(self, value):
        from quack.cute_dsl_utils import torch2cute_dtype_map

        # head_dim must be static in the fake (begin() does layout algebra on it).
        return (torch2cute_dtype_map[value.dtype], value.shape[-1])

    def host_fake_arg(self, key, fctx):
        from quack.compile_utils import make_fake_tensor

        dtype, head_dim = key
        return make_fake_tensor(
            dtype, (cute.sym_int(), head_dim), leading_dim=1, divisibility=128 // dtype.width
        )


class RotaryCosSinTMALoad(TileLoad):
    """The (seqlen_ro, head_dim) interleaved cos/sin table staged through the
    TMA epilogue load pipeline instead of per-tile gmem->rmem copies
    (RotaryCosSinLoad). Default choice — see ``rotary_cos_sin_load``.

    TMA descriptors cannot encode the stride-0 head broadcast, so the wrap
    lives in the copy COORDINATES: each epi subtile TMA-loads the table box
    at column ``output_col % head_dim`` (redundant loads across heads hit L2).
    The smem stage then holds exactly the subtile-aligned cos/sin slice, so
    the whole TileLoad consumer path (S2R, staging, pipeline tx accounting)
    is inherited unchanged. Dense-only for now (TMA loads have no varlen_m
    ragged-descriptor path; use the LDG op under varlen).
    """

    def __init__(self, name):
        super().__init__(name)

    def host_arg_key(self, value):
        from quack.cute_dsl_utils import torch2cute_dtype_map

        # head_dim static in the fake: the copy fn branches on it at trace time.
        return (torch2cute_dtype_map[value.dtype], value.shape[-1])

    def host_fake_arg(self, key, fctx):
        from quack.compile_utils import make_fake_tensor

        dtype, head_dim = key
        return make_fake_tensor(
            dtype, (cute.sym_int(), head_dim), leading_dim=1, divisibility=128 // dtype.width
        )

    def load_g2s_copy_fn(
        self,
        gemm,
        params,
        smem_tensor,
        tile_coord_mnkl,
        varlen_manager,
        epi_pipeline,
    ):
        assert not varlen_manager.varlen_m, (
            "RotaryCosSinTMALoad does not support varlen_m; use "
            "rotary_cos_sin_load(name, tma=False) (rope_table_ldg_epi / qk_rope_ldg_epi)"
        )
        # The TMA prep appends a stride-0 batch mode; slice it off (all
        # batches share the table).
        tensor = varlen_manager.offset_batch_epi(getattr(params, self.name), tile_coord_mnkl[3])
        head_dim = const_expr(tensor.shape[1])
        tile_M, tile_N = gemm.cta_tile_shape_mnk[0], gemm.cta_tile_shape_mnk[1]
        epi_tile = getattr(params, self._epi_tile_key())
        epi_N = const_expr(cute.size(epi_tile[1]))
        atom = getattr(params, self._tma_atom_key())
        if const_expr(tile_N % head_dim == 0):
            # Tile covers >= 1 whole head: tile the table (tile_M, head_dim)
            # and wrap the epi-subtile N coordinate modulo subtiles-per-head.
            assert head_dim % epi_N == 0, "head_dim must be a multiple of the epi tile N"
            subtiles_per_head = const_expr(head_dim // epi_N)
            copy_tile_fn, _, _ = gemm.epilog_gmem_copy_and_partition(
                atom,
                tensor,
                (tile_M, head_dim),
                epi_tile,
                smem_tensor,
                (tile_coord_mnkl[0], 0),
            )
            inner = copy_utils.tma_producer_copy_fn(copy_tile_fn, epi_pipeline)
            # Callers pass either the hier (epi_m, epi_n) coord (gemm_base's
            # inline path) or a linear subtile index (the SM100 dedicated
            # epi-load warp): decode linear via the same ordered layout the
            # store loop uses so pipeline stage order matches consumption.
            epi_tile_shape = cute.zipped_divide(
                cute.make_layout(gemm.cta_tile_shape_mnk[:2]), epi_tile
            ).shape[1]
            epi_tile_layout = cute.make_ordered_layout(
                epi_tile_shape, order=(0, 1) if const_expr(gemm.epi_m_major) else (1, 0)
            )

            def copy_fn(src_idx, producer_state, **kw):
                coord = (
                    src_idx
                    if isinstance(src_idx, tuple)
                    else epi_tile_layout.get_hier_coord(src_idx)
                )
                inner((coord[0], coord[1] % subtiles_per_head), producer_state, **kw)

            return copy_fn
        # A head spans several tiles: pick the head-relative N tile, no
        # per-subtile wrap needed.
        assert head_dim % tile_N == 0, (
            "rotary epilogue requires tile_N to be a multiple or a divisor of head_dim"
        )
        copy_tile_fn, _, _ = gemm.epilog_gmem_copy_and_partition(
            atom,
            tensor,
            (tile_M, tile_N),
            epi_tile,
            smem_tensor,
            (tile_coord_mnkl[0], tile_coord_mnkl[1] % (head_dim // tile_N)),
        )
        return copy_utils.tma_producer_copy_fn(copy_tile_fn, epi_pipeline)


def rotary_cos_sin_load(name, tma=True):
    """Rotary cos/sin table op. ``tma=True`` (default) stages the table via
    the TMA epilogue load pipeline; ``tma=False`` is the per-tile gmem->rmem
    op — required for varlen_m and pre-TMA archs (SM80), and 1-3% faster at
    large non-pingpong tiles.

    Why TMA is the default — H100, m=16384 k=4096 head_dim=128, rope overhead
    vs an identity epilogue at the same config (interleaved-median bench):

    ==================  =======  =======
    config              LDG      TMA
    ==================  =======  =======
    256x128 c(1,2)      +15.3%   +15.5%   best PLAIN-GEMM config
    128x256 c(1,1)      +13.6%   +10.0%
    128x128 c(1,2) pp    +6.2%    +1.7%
    192x128 c(1,2) pp    +4.3%    +1.3%   best rope/qknorm config
    ==================  =======  =======

    Under pingpong the producer-warp TMA staging escapes the exclusive
    per-warpgroup epilogue window that serializes consumer LDGs; at 192-row
    pingpong tiles the LDG double-buffer register cost tips composed
    epilogues into spills (qk_rope: LDG +23% vs TMA +2.5%). Clustered
    pingpong + TMA is the absolute winner for the fused QK-norm/RoPE
    epilogues (qk_rope 794us vs 918us at the best non-pingpong config), so
    the default optimizes the configs these epilogues actually run on.
    """
    return RotaryCosSinTMALoad(name) if tma else RotaryCosSinLoadHost(name)


@gemm_epilogue(ops={"cs": rotary_cos_sin_load("cs")}, mode="acc_pair")
def rope_table_epi(acc, cs, bias):
    """RoPE from the real (seqlen, head_dim) table op, composed with a rowvec
    bias in fn math — the op is a value port; rotation order is explicit."""
    x1, x2 = unpack(acc + bias)
    c, s = unpack(cs)
    return {"D": pack(x1 * c - x2 * s, x1 * s + x2 * c)}


@gemm_epilogue(ops={"cs": rotary_cos_sin_load("cs", tma=False)}, mode="acc_pair")
def rope_table_ldg_epi(acc, cs, bias):
    """rope_table_epi on the gmem->rmem table op: required for varlen_m
    (table indexed by global flattened row), pre-TMA archs, and marginally
    faster at large non-pingpong tiles (see rotary_cos_sin_load)."""
    x1, x2 = unpack(acc + bias)
    c, s = unpack(cs)
    return {"D": pack(x1 * c - x2 * s, x1 * s + x2 * c)}


@gemm_epilogue(ops={"pos": ColVecLoad("pos"), "freq": RowVecLoad("freq")}, mode="acc_pair")
def rope_posfreq_epi(acc, pos, freq):
    """RoPE computing cos/sin in-kernel via ``sincos(pos * inv_freq)`` instead
    of loading the precomputed (seqlen_ro, head_dim) table.

    ``pos`` is the per-row position, (l, m) float32 (exact up to 2^24; may
    differ per batch, unlike the shared table). ``freq`` is the per-output-
    column inv-freq as a float-float table, (l, n) float32, hi at even
    columns and lo at odd (same interleaving convention as the cos/sin
    table) — build it with ``make_interleaved_inv_freq``. Both are plain
    broadcast vector loads, so the per-tile gmem traffic is tile_M + tile_N
    elements vs the table's tile_M * head_dim; the table's tile_N/head_dim
    alignment constraint disappears (the head wrap is baked into the freq
    table), and varlen_m works for free (rank-1 (total_m,) ``pos``).
    Per-column behavior is data, not kernel structure: zero-frequency columns
    rotate by angle 0, an exact identity, so packed QKV projections rotate
    only the Q/K block via ``make_interleaved_inv_freq(inv_freq, qk_dim,
    v_dim)`` — no branch, V passes through bitwise.

    Angle math: the f32 product pos*freq loses absolute precision linearly in
    the angle (a plain-f32 pipeline — including a table built from f32 host
    angles — is off by 5e-3 of output scale at 128k positions, 0.67 at 16M),
    so the angle is computed as a float-float, in TURNS: the table stores
    inv_freq/2pi, the reduction is an exact mod-1 (H100's MUFU natively works
    in turns — ptxas prepends an FMUL.RZ by 1/2pi to every ``sin.approx``, so
    reducing mod 2pi in radians is the same work in the wrong unit; mod-1
    needs no Cody-Waite constant split at all). Max error vs an f64 reference
    is ~8e-7 of output scale at every position range through 2^24 — same as a
    table built from f64 host angles (checked: in-kernel libdevice sincosf
    gains nothing and costs +17-65% kernel time). Pipe budget per rotation
    pair: 15 FMA-pipe ops + 2 MUFU — the quarter-rate XU pipe (MUFU) is the
    epilogue's math wall, which is why the round uses the magic-bias adds
    instead of FRND (FRND also issues on XU; evicting it cut the exposed
    k=512 rope overhead by ~4-6pp, ncu-verified). H100 m=16384 k=4096 n=4096
    head_dim=128, overhead vs a bias-only epilogue at the same config
    (interleaved-median bench), against rope_table_epi's TMA table:

    ==================  ========  =======
    config              posfreq   table
    ==================  ========  =======
    192x128 c(1,2) pp     +0.8%    +2.0%
    128x256 c(1,1)        +3.8%    +4.8%
    256x128 c(1,2)        +4.2%   +10.8%
    ==================  ========  =======
    """
    # Reference math, per rotation pair (x1, x2) at row position `pos`:
    #     theta = pos * inv_freq
    #     D = (x1*cos(theta) - x2*sin(theta), x1*sin(theta) + x2*cos(theta))
    # The angle helpers below compute this with three transformations that
    # lose no accuracy (turns units, float-float compensation, magic-bias
    # rounding) — see _angle_turns / _sincos_turns for the derivations.
    x1, x2 = unpack(acc)
    s, c = _sincos_turns(*_angle_turns(pos, freq))
    return {"D": pack(x1 * c - x2 * s, x1 * s + x2 * c)}


@gemm_epilogue(ops={"pos": ColVecLoad("pos"), "freq": RowVecLoad("freq")}, mode="acc_pair")
def rope_posfreq_bias_epi(acc, pos, freq, bias):
    """rope_posfreq_epi with a rowvec bias added before the rotation (biased
    QKV projections; a separate mod because an absent operand must be absent
    from the signature to compile the term out)."""
    x1, x2 = unpack(acc + bias)
    s, c = _sincos_turns(*_angle_turns(pos, freq))
    return {"D": pack(x1 * c - x2 * s, x1 * s + x2 * c)}


@gemm_epilogue(
    ops={"pos": ColVecLoad("pos"), "freq": RowVecLoad("freq"), "rstd": ColVecLoad("rstd")},
    mode="acc_pair",
)
def rstd_rope_posfreq_epi(acc, pos, freq, rstd):
    """Mid-stack QKV epilogue of a Coda-style transformer block (deferred-rstd
    boundary): scale rows by the boundary's rstd colvec (the producing GEMM
    wrote a = h*gamma with the rstd deferred here — a row scale commutes
    through the GEMM), then rotate. Rope applies to the Q/K columns and V
    passes through bitwise via zero-frequency columns of the interleaved freq
    table (see rope_posfreq_epi; the row scale commutes with the rotation, so
    scaling before unpack is exact)."""
    x1, x2 = unpack(acc * rstd)
    s, c = _sincos_turns(*_angle_turns(pos, freq))
    return {"D": pack(x1 * c - x2 * s, x1 * s + x2 * c)}


def _angle_turns(pos, freq):
    """theta = pos * inv_freq as an unevaluated float-float sum (t, lo), in
    TURNS (the freq table stores inv_freq/2pi — see make_interleaved_inv_freq).

    The plain product pos*fh rounds away low bits worth whole rotations once
    pos*freq is large (~0.5 ulp = 1 rotation at pos ~ 2^24, freq ~ 1). The
    exact FFMA residual of the product plus the below-f32 freq bits (fl)
    carry them in the compensation term `lo`, re-added after range reduction
    when the angle is small again (_sincos_turns)."""
    fh, fl = unpack(freq)  # float-float inv_freq/2pi: fh + fl to ~2^-49 rel
    t = pos * fh  # angle in turns, rounded to f32
    terr = cute.math.fma(pos, fh, -t)  # bits the product rounded away (exact)
    lo = cute.math.fma(pos, fl, terr)  # + the angle bits below fh's precision
    return t, lo


def _sincos_turns(t, lo):
    """(sin, cos) of the float-float angle (t + lo) turns via MUFU.

    Turns make range reduction exact: theta mod 1 is a round and a subtract,
    no Cody-Waite constant splitting — and turns are the hardware's native
    unit (MUFU.SIN takes turns; ptxas prepends x*(1/2pi) to every radians
    sin.approx). The round uses the magic-bias add because MUFU.SIN/COS and
    FRND all issue on the quarter-rate XU pipe, the epilogue's math
    bottleneck (the 2 MUFU are its floor) — full-rate FMA-pipe ops beat FRND
    (B300 128x256 k=512 exposed overhead vs bias-only: +47.7% vs +49.5%)."""
    # Round-to-nearest-even via the magic bias: exact for |t| < 2^22 (here
    # t < 2^24/2pi), because adding 1.5*2^23 shifts the integer part onto the
    # mantissa boundary. t - q is then exact (both are multiples of ulp(t)).
    # The biasing add is written as a math-dialect fma (t*1.0 + M, bitwise
    # identical to t + M; ptxas strength-reduces it back to FADD) so the
    # SM100 loop vectorizer scalarizes it: written as arith `(t + M) - M`,
    # t gets two vectorized-arith consumers, the dataflow shape that
    # heap-corrupts the closed vectorizer pass (segfault/double-free/compile
    # hang; minimal repro `pack(x1 + t, x2 + t)`). Same reason the sin/cos
    # below are separate calls, not the fused two-result cute.math.sincos.
    q = cute.math.fma(t, 1.0, 12582912.0) - 12582912.0
    r = (t - q) + lo  # theta mod 1, plus the compensation term
    # sin.approx wants radians and ptxas rescales by 1/2pi for MUFU; the
    # cancelling multiply pair is PTX's toll — there is no turns-domain PTX.
    # Separate sin/cos calls, NOT cute.math.sincos: the SM100 loop vectorizer
    # (the vectorize=True pair loop in gemm_epilogue) segfaults the MLIR
    # compiler on the fused two-result op. Identical SASS either way — ptxas
    # shares the FMUL.RZ between the MUFU.SIN/MUFU.COS pair of one argument.
    r_rad = r * 6.283185307179586
    s = cute.math.sin(r_rad, fastmath=True)
    c = cute.math.cos(r_rad, fastmath=True)
    return s, c


@gemm_epilogue(ops={"pos": ColVecLoad("pos"), "freq": RowVecLoad("freq")}, mode="acc_pair")
def rope_posfreq_scaled_epi(acc, pos, freq, bias, scale):
    """rope_posfreq_epi with an attention-temperature factor on the rotated
    output: D = scale * rope(acc + bias). This is YaRN's mscale (DeepSeek-V2/
    V3, Qwen long-context) — the table-op form bakes it into the host cos/sin
    values, but with in-kernel sincos it must be a multiply (an angle change
    cannot express a magnitude change), so it costs one Scalar operand and
    two FMULs per pair. The YaRN frequency transform itself is pure data:
    feed the transformed inv_freq to make_interleaved_inv_freq."""
    x1, x2 = unpack(acc + bias)
    s, c = _sincos_turns(*_angle_turns(pos, freq))
    x1, x2 = x1 * scale, x2 * scale
    return {"D": pack(x1 * c - x2 * s, x1 * s + x2 * c)}


@gemm_epilogue(
    ops={
        "pos_t": ColVecLoad("pos_t"),
        "pos_h": ColVecLoad("pos_h"),
        "pos_w": ColVecLoad("pos_w"),
        "freq_t": RowVecLoad("freq_t"),
        "freq_h": RowVecLoad("freq_h"),
        "freq_w": RowVecLoad("freq_w"),
    },
    mode="acc_pair",
)
def mrope_posfreq_epi(acc, pos_t, pos_h, pos_w, freq_t, freq_h, freq_w, bias):
    """Multimodal 3D RoPE (Qwen2-VL mRoPE): head-dim sections rotate by
    different position axes — pair j uses pos_t, pos_h, or pos_w according to
    which section j falls in. The section SELECT is data, not kernel
    structure: each axis gets its own freq table, zeroed outside its section
    (make_mrope_inv_freq), so the angle is the three-term dot product

        theta = pos_t*f_t(j) + pos_h*f_h(j) + pos_w*f_w(j)

    with exactly one nonzero term per column — the sums are exact (adding
    zeros), so the float-float compensation of the live term survives intact.
    Costs two extra vector-load pairs and ~6 FMA-pipe ops per pair over
    rope_posfreq_epi; the XU (MUFU) cost is unchanged."""
    x1, x2 = unpack(acc + bias)
    t1, lo1 = _angle_turns(pos_t, freq_t)
    t2, lo2 = _angle_turns(pos_h, freq_h)
    t3, lo3 = _angle_turns(pos_w, freq_w)
    # The t sums are math-dialect fmas (bitwise == the adds), NOT arith `+`:
    # each t_i already feeds its Dekker negf, and a second vectorized-arith
    # consumer is the SM100 vectorizer's crash shape (see _sincos_turns).
    # The lo_i are math.fma results — their arith sums are single-consumer
    # and pack fine.
    t12 = cute.math.fma(t1, 1.0, t2)
    t = cute.math.fma(t3, 1.0, t12)
    s, c = _sincos_turns(t, (lo1 + lo2) + lo3)
    return {"D": pack(x1 * c - x2 * s, x1 * s + x2 * c)}


@gemm_epilogue(
    ops={
        "pos": ColVecLoad("pos"),
        "dpos": ColVecLoad("dpos"),
        "freq": RowVecLoad("freq"),
        "logz": RowVecLoad("logz"),
    },
    mode="acc_pair",
)
def xpos_posfreq_epi(acc, pos, dpos, freq, logz, bias):
    """xPos (length-extrapolatable RoPE, Sun et al. 2022): the rope_posfreq
    rotation times a per-pair magnitude decay zeta_j**dpos.

    xPos REQUIRES OPPOSITE scales on Q and K — query zeta^(+m/s), key
    zeta^(-m/s), so the attention score decays as zeta^((m-n)/s) — and that
    sign lives in the DATA, not in two kernels: ``logz`` carries per-column
    log2(zeta_j) (make_xpos_log_scale), positive over Q columns, negative
    over K, zero over V (exp2(0) = 1, so the packed-QKV passthrough
    survives). ``dpos`` is the decay exponent, typically
    (pos - offset) / scale_base — a separate colvec from the rotation
    position because implementations offset/rescale it to keep zeta**dpos in
    f32 range. Costs one MUFU.EX2 per pair: the quarter-rate XU pipe goes
    from 2 to 3 ops/pair, so expect ~1.5x plain rope's exposed-epilogue
    overhead (hidden regimes unaffected)."""
    x1, x2 = unpack(acc + bias)
    s, c = _sincos_turns(*_angle_turns(pos, freq))
    z, _ = unpack(logz)  # both lanes of a pair share the decay
    zeta = cute.math.exp2(dpos * z, fastmath=True)
    x1, x2 = x1 * zeta, x2 * zeta
    return {"D": pack(x1 * c - x2 * s, x1 * s + x2 * c)}


def _ff_turns_head(inv_freq):
    """(head,) float-float split of inv_freq/2pi, interleaved hi/lo per pair."""
    import math

    import torch

    f64 = inv_freq.double() / (2 * math.pi)
    hi = f64.float()
    lo = (f64 - hi.double()).float()
    return torch.stack([hi, lo], dim=-1).reshape(-1)


def make_interleaved_inv_freq(inv_freq, rotary_n, nonrotary_n=0, head_dim=None):
    """Pack HF-style inv_freq (rotary_dim/2,) into the (rotary_n + nonrotary_n,)
    float-float table rope_posfreq_epi consumes: rotation pair j of each head
    reads (hi, lo) at columns (2j, 2j+1), where hi + lo is the two-float32
    split of inv_freq[j] / 2pi — the kernel's angle unit is TURNS (see
    rope_posfreq_epi) — with heads repeating the pattern over the first
    rotary_n columns. Zero frequency means angle 0, an exact identity (MUFU
    sincos(0) is exactly (0, 1)), which encodes the popular non-rotated
    layouts as data:

    * packed QKV — RoPE on Q/K, V passed through bitwise: the last
      nonrotary_n columns are zero-frequency;
      ``make_interleaved_inv_freq(inv_freq, q_dim + k_dim, v_dim)``.
    * partial rotary (GPT-J / Phi / GLM: rotary_dim < head_dim) — pass
      ``head_dim``: each head's tail beyond 2*len(inv_freq) is zero-frequency.

    NTK-aware scaling (fixed or dynamic) and YaRN's NTK-by-parts ramp are
    pure inv_freq transforms — pass the transformed values here (YaRN's
    mscale additionally needs rope_posfreq_scaled_epi).

    The split preserves inv_freq/2pi to ~2^-49 relative precision — pass
    inv_freq as float64 if available; float32 input still splits exactly (the
    /2pi quotient is computed in f64), only the input's own quantization is
    unrecoverable."""
    import torch

    head = _ff_turns_head(inv_freq)
    rotary_dim = head.shape[0]
    head_dim = rotary_dim if head_dim is None else head_dim
    assert head_dim >= rotary_dim and head_dim % 2 == 0
    head = torch.nn.functional.pad(head, (0, head_dim - rotary_dim))
    assert rotary_n % head_dim == 0, "rotary_n must be a whole number of heads"
    assert nonrotary_n % 2 == 0, "nonrotary_n must be even (columns are processed in pairs)"
    return torch.nn.functional.pad(head.repeat(rotary_n // head_dim), (0, nonrotary_n))


def make_mrope_inv_freq(inv_freq, sections, rotary_n, nonrotary_n=0):
    """Per-axis freq tables for mrope_posfreq_epi (Qwen2-VL mRoPE).

    ``sections`` is the pairs-per-axis split of the head (HF mrope_section,
    e.g. (16, 24, 24) for head_dim 128); axis a's table carries inv_freq/2pi
    over its own section's pairs and zero elsewhere, so the kernel's
    three-term angle dot product selects the right position axis per column
    purely through the data. Returns len(sections) tables shaped like
    make_interleaved_inv_freq's output."""
    import torch

    assert sum(sections) == inv_freq.shape[0], "sections must cover all rotation pairs"
    head = _ff_turns_head(inv_freq)
    head_dim = head.shape[0]
    assert rotary_n % head_dim == 0, "rotary_n must be a whole number of heads"
    assert nonrotary_n % 2 == 0, "nonrotary_n must be even (columns are processed in pairs)"
    outs = []
    start = 0
    for sec in sections:
        masked = torch.zeros_like(head)
        masked[2 * start : 2 * (start + sec)] = head[2 * start : 2 * (start + sec)]
        outs.append(torch.nn.functional.pad(masked.repeat(rotary_n // head_dim), (0, nonrotary_n)))
        start += sec
    return tuple(outs)


def make_xpos_log_scale(head_dim, q_n, k_n=0, nonscaled_n=0, gamma=0.4, device=None):
    """Per-column log2(zeta) table for xpos_posfreq_epi.

    zeta_j = (2j + gamma*head_dim) / ((1 + gamma)*head_dim) per rotation pair
    (the torchscale convention, gamma=0.4). The first q_n columns get
    +log2(zeta) (query side, decay zeta^+dpos), the next k_n get -log2(zeta)
    (key side, zeta^-dpos), the last nonscaled_n get 0 (exp2(0) = 1 — the V
    block of a packed QKV projection passes through unscaled). For separate
    Q / K projections build two tables (q_n=n / k_n=n)."""
    import torch

    assert q_n % head_dim == 0 and k_n % head_dim == 0, "q_n/k_n must be whole heads"
    assert nonscaled_n % 2 == 0, "nonscaled_n must be even (columns are processed in pairs)"
    j2 = torch.arange(0, head_dim, 2, dtype=torch.float64, device=device)
    zeta = (j2 + gamma * head_dim) / ((1 + gamma) * head_dim)
    logz = torch.log2(zeta).float().repeat_interleave(2)  # both pair lanes share it
    return torch.cat(
        [
            logz.repeat(q_n // head_dim),
            -logz.repeat(k_n // head_dim),
            logz.new_zeros(nonscaled_n),
        ]
    )


def make_interleaved_cos_sin(cos, sin):
    """Interleave HF-style cos/sin (seqlen_ro, head_dim/2) into the
    (seqlen_ro, head_dim) table RotaryCosSinLoad consumes (cos at even
    columns, sin at odd). From the epirope hand-written kernel."""
    import torch

    assert cos.shape == sin.shape and cos.ndim == 2
    return torch.stack([cos, sin], dim=-1).reshape(cos.shape[0], -1).contiguous()

# Copyright (c) 2026, Tri Dao.
"""Per-head rstd statistics for composed GEMM epilogues."""

from __future__ import annotations

import cutlass.cute as cute
from cutlass import Float32, const_expr

from quack.epilogue.ops import GroupedColStatsBase


class HeadRstd(GroupedColStatsBase):
    """Per-(row, head) rstd value port — pure statistics, no weight.

    The prepass fn returns the SQUARED values under this op's name, the base
    add-combine fold sums them per (row, head) (deterministic, no float
    atomics), and ``stat_value`` finalizes rsqrt(mean + eps). Apply it in the
    epilogue fn: ``acc * rstd``, or ``acc * rstd * w`` with the norm weight
    as an independent RowVecLoad (pass it (N,)-shaped, i.e. the head weight
    repeated per head). Host arg: head_dim as a plain int, or any 1-D
    (head_dim,) tensor — only its LENGTH is used (it fixes the group
    width)."""

    def __init__(self, name, eps=1e-6):
        super().__init__(name)
        self.eps = eps

    def config_key(self):
        return (self.eps,)

    @cute.jit
    def stat_value(self, total, group_cols):
        inv_d = const_expr(1.0 / group_cols)
        return cute.math.rsqrt(total * inv_d + Float32(self.eps), fastmath=True)

19	SM120 a vec-32 row SFD normally widens the tiled-MMA warp run to 32
20	contiguous N columns (GemmSm120.mma_n_warp_run) so the whole SF vector is

139	    (sf_vec_size = 32 for e8m0 scales, 16 for e4m3 scales, contiguous along N),
140	    quantizes ``scale = amax / d_dtype_max * norm_const`` to the SF dtype
141	    (f32->e8m0 rounds up, f32->e4m3 rounds to nearest even — hardware cvt
142	    semantics, same as the CUTLASS C++ Sm100BlockScaleFactorRowStore), and
143	    rescales tRS_rD in place by ``min(norm_const * rcp(dequant(SF)), FLT_MAX)``
144	    so the downstream fp32 -> d_dtype conversion produces the quantized values.
145	
146	    SF bytes for the whole CTA tile are kept in registers and written to gmem
147	    once per tile in ``end`` with plain vectorized stores (the 128x4 SF atom
148	    puts 4 consecutive SF slots of a row at consecutive bytes, so a full row
149	    flushes as 4-byte stores). No TMA; smem only for the cross-warp amax
150	    exchange on SM120 warp-MMA layouts (see the smem hooks below).
151	
152	    The gmem tensor is the blocked (L, rm, rk, 32, 4, 4) scale layout shared
153	    with SFA/SFB; ``to_params`` re-views it with the logical (M_pad, N_pad, L)
154	    layout whose intra-vector mode has stride 0, so it can be tiled and
155	    partitioned exactly like D. Register/gmem slot pairing needs no assumption
156	    on the fragment order: SF slots live in a zero-stride-broadcast register
157	    tensor partitioned the same way as tRS_rD (the VecReduce trick), and
158	    ``filter_zeros`` on both sides yields matching slot orders.
159	
160	    Bounds: SF storage is padded to 128-row x 4-slot atoms, so M is either
161	    fully covered or fully out for a CTA (tile_M and the padded extent are both
162	    multiples of 128 per CTA). Along N: when tile_N covers whole SF atom
163	    columns (tile_N % (4 * vec) == 0), the gmem view is CTA-tiled and a fully
164	    in-bounds tile flushes with one autovec copy; otherwise (or for a partial
165	    last N tile) the flush runs per epi subtile with a uniform bounds check —
166	    every epi subtile N width divides the atom coverage, so each subtile is
167	    either fully inside or fully outside the padded SF extent.
168	    """
169	
170	    def __init__(self, name, direction="row", output="D"):
171	        """direction selects the SF vector orientation: "row" = vec contiguous
172	        elements along N (output feeds the next GEMM's K = this N), "col" =
173	        vec contiguous elements along M (for backward, where the consumer
174	        contracts over this output's M). "col" quantization reduces across
175	        lanes: on SM100, with the (4,1) epilogue warp shape and the 32dp32b
176	        tmem load, lane == row within a warp's 32-row stripe, so an SF vector
177	        of 32 (16) rows is exactly one warp (half-warp) — a butterfly-shuffle
178	        max per column, no smem, SF bytes stored per byte by a designated
179	        lane (adjacent columns' bytes are 16 B apart in the transposed atom,
180	        so no packing is possible — CUTLASS ColStore behaves the same). On
181	        SM120 col runs the generic slot machinery with the vector axis
182	        along M (stride-4 lane groups, warp_m-pair smem exchange).
183	
184	        output: which stored output this codec quantizes. "D" (default) is
185	        the main output; a minted-mod output name (e.g. "postact") quantizes
186	        that aux output instead. Either way the driver's store loop calls
187	        :meth:`quantize` on the output's final fragment right before its
188	        store op converts to the storage dtype (see gemm_base.epilogue).
189	        For gated (acc_pair) aux outputs the SF slots live in ACCUMULATOR
190	        space — postact column j comes from acc columns {2j, 2j+1}, so one
191	        SF vector of ``vec`` postact values spans ``2 * vec`` acc columns
192	        (vec_acc below) and the fragment indexes its slot at acc_stride * i.
193	        The gmem SF atom layout is vec-agnostic, so only the broadcast factor
194	        changes.
195	        """
196	        super().__init__(name)
197	        assert direction in ("row", "col")
198	        assert output == "D" or direction == "row", "aux quantization is row-direction only"
199	        self.direction = direction
200	        self.quant_output = output
201	
202	    def config_key(self):
203	        return (self.direction, self.quant_output)
204	
205	    def _col_redux_path(self, arch):
206	        """Whether the col direction takes SM100's dedicated implementation
207	        instead of the generic slot machinery. Justified fork, not incidental:
208	        the SM100 tmem-load geometry puts lane == row, so each column's amax
209	        is ONE redux.sync.max.abs.NaN.f32 (SM100-family instruction) and SF
210	        bytes store inline per subtile — whole-tile register accumulation
211	        would need one slot byte per fragment element (every column is its
212	        own slot; nothing aliases). SM120's warp-MMA fragments spread each
213	        column over stride-4 lane groups and 16-row warp stripes, so col
214	        rides the generic butterfly + sExch path there. ``arch`` may be None
215	        (arch-less smem budgeting): treated as non-SM100."""
216	        return self.direction == "col" and arch == 100
217	
218	    def host_fake_arg(self, key, fctx):
219	        # Blocked (L, rm, rk, 32, 4, 4) fake; varlen_m SFD is one M-padded
220	        # buffer with a static batch dim of 1 (same convention as input SFA).
221	        dtype, ndim = key
222	        assert ndim == 6, f"SFD expects a 6-D blocked scale tensor, got ndim {ndim}"
223	        return make_fake_sf_tensor(dtype, 1 if fctx.varlen_m else fctx.l)
224	
225	    def _vec_attr(self):
226	        return f"_sf_vec_{self.name}"
227	
228	    def _sf_dtype_attr(self):
229	        return f"_sf_dtype_{self.name}"
230	
231	    def _val_dtype_attr(self):
232	        return f"_sf_val_dtype_{self.name}"
233	
234	    def _acc_mult_attr(self):
235	        return f"_sf_acc_mult_{self.name}"
236	
237	    def to_params(self, gemm, args):
238	        mSFD = getattr(args, self.name)
239	        # The optional fp32 norm constant (reciprocal of the nvfp4 per-tensor
240	        # scale) is THIS op's parameter: pair it into the param so the device
241	        # hooks are self-contained. The EpilogueArguments field stays flat
242	        # (host FFI schemas carry no tuples).
243	        norm_const = getattr(args, "sfd_norm_const", None)
244	        sf_dtype = mSFD.element_type
245	        if self.quant_output == "D":
246	            val_dtype, val_layout = gemm.d_dtype, gemm.d_layout
247	            acc_mult = 1
248	        else:
249	            # Aux-output quantization: the value tensor is the owning
250	            # TileStore's arg; a gated (acc_pair) output pairs adjacent
251	            # accumulator columns, so one postact column covers 2 acc columns.
252	            val_tensor = getattr(args, self.quant_output)
253	            val_dtype = val_tensor.element_type
254	            val_layout = cutlass.utils.LayoutEnum.from_tensor(val_tensor)
255	            store = next(
256	                op for op in gemm._epi_ops if op.is_tile_store() and op.name == self.quant_output
257	            )
258	            acc_mult = 2 if store.gated else 1
259	            assert not getattr(gemm, "_epi_mod_packed_cd", False), (
260	                "aux quantization does not support packed_cd mods"
261	            )
262	        # Both directions and aux-output (postact) quantization run on the
263	        # SM100 tmem epilogue and the SM90-style register epilogue (SM120
264	        # warp MMA).
265	        assert gemm.arch in (100, 120), (
266	            "Quantized output (SFD) is only supported on SM100/SM120 for now"
267	        )
268	        assert sf_dtype in (cutlass.Float8E8M0FNU, cutlass.Float8E4M3FN), (
269	            f"SFD dtype must be e8m0 (mx) or e4m3 (nvfp4), got {sf_dtype}"
270	        )
271	        vec = sf_vec_size_for(sf_dtype)
272	        assert val_dtype in QUANT_DTYPE_MAX, (
273	            f"Quantized output requires fp8/fp4 values, got {val_dtype}"
274	        )
275	        assert not (sf_dtype is cutlass.Float8E4M3FN and val_dtype is not cutlass.Float4E2M1FN), (
276	            "e4m3 scale factors (nvfp4) require Float4E2M1FN output"
277	        )
278	        assert val_layout.is_n_major_c(), "Quantized output requires row-major (N-major) values"
279	        assert gemm.acc_dtype is Float32, "Quantized output requires fp32 accumulation"
280	        assert not (gemm.cta_tile_shape_mnk[0] == 64 and getattr(gemm, "use_2cta_instrs", False)), (
281	            "Quantized output (SFD) requires the (4,1) epilogue warp shape: the 64-row "
282	            "2-CTA tile splits SF vectors across threads (use tile_m 256 or cluster_m 1)"
283	        )
284	        if self.direction == "col":
285	            return self._to_params_col(gemm, mSFD, sf_dtype, vec, norm_const)
286	        # The op works entirely in accumulator-N space: identity for D, and
287	        # acc_mult * vec consecutive acc columns per SF vector for a gated
288	        # aux target (postact interleaves gate/up at pair granularity).
289	        vec_acc = vec * acc_mult
290	        assert gemm.cta_tile_shape_mnk[1] % vec_acc == 0
291	        epi_tile_n = gemm.epi_tile[1]
292	        # Each SF vector must be produced within a single epilogue subtile: the
293	        # contiguous N run of a subtile must cover whole SF vectors. epi_tile_n
294	        # is an int shape normally, or a strided layout from the non-pow2
295	        # tile_n fixup in which case mode 0 is the contiguous run.
296	        if isinstance(epi_tile_n, cute.Layout):
297	            shape = epi_tile_n.shape
298	            epi_n_run = shape if isinstance(shape, int) else shape[0]
299	        else:
300	            epi_n_run = cute.size(epi_tile_n)
301	        assert epi_n_run % vec_acc == 0, (
302	            f"epi tile N run ({epi_n_run}) must cover whole SF vectors of {vec_acc} acc columns"
303	        )
304	        setattr(gemm, self._vec_attr(), vec_acc)
305	        setattr(gemm, self._sf_dtype_attr(), sf_dtype)
306	        setattr(gemm, self._val_dtype_attr(), val_dtype)
307	        setattr(gemm, self._acc_mult_attr(), acc_mult)
308	        # (L, rm, rk, 32, 4, 4) blocked scale tensor -> logical (M_pad, N_pad, L)
309	        # view with the hardware 128x4 SF atom and stride-0 intra-vector mode
310	        # (N_pad in ACC columns: rk * 4 slots * vec_acc — the 512 B atom is
311	        # vec-agnostic, only the broadcast factor differs for gated aux).
312	        # For varlen_m the buffer is one M-padded (1, total_padded_rm, rk)
313	        # region (tile-aligned per-batch padding, same convention as input
314	        # SFA); build a rank-2 view so offset_batch_SFA's compound-coord tile
315	        # shift applies.
316	        m_pad = mSFD.shape[1] * 128
317	        n_pad = mSFD.shape[2] * vec_acc * 4
318	        if getattr(gemm, "varlen_m", False):
319	            sfd_shape = (m_pad, n_pad)
320	        else:
321	            sfd_shape = (m_pad, n_pad, mSFD.shape[0])
322	        sfd_layout = layout_utils.tile_atom_to_shape_SF_strided(sfd_shape, vec_acc, mSFD.stride)
323	        return {self.name: (cute.make_tensor(mSFD.iterator, sfd_layout), norm_const)}
324	
325	    def _to_params_col(self, gemm, mSFD, sf_dtype, vec, norm_const):
326	        """Column-direction SF: vectors of `vec` rows along M. The blocked
327	        tensor is (L, rn, rm_k, 32, 4, 4) — 128-column atoms with rm_k
328	        4-slot groups along M. Build a logical (M_pad, N_pad, L) view whose
329	        M mode broadcasts over the vec rows sharing one SF byte."""
330	        assert not getattr(gemm, "varlen_m", False) and not getattr(gemm, "varlen_k", False), (
331	            "Column-direction SFD does not support varlen yet"
332	        )
333	        if gemm.arch == 120:
334	            # The slot machinery produces each SF vector within one epilogue
335	            # subtile; its M extent must cover whole vec-row vectors.
336	            epi_m = cute.size(cute.shape(gemm.epi_tile[0]))
337	            assert epi_m % vec == 0, (
338	                f"epi tile M ({epi_m}) must cover whole SF vectors of {vec} rows"
339	            )
340	        setattr(gemm, self._vec_attr(), vec)
341	        setattr(gemm, self._sf_dtype_attr(), sf_dtype)
342	        setattr(gemm, self._val_dtype_attr(), gemm.d_dtype)
343	        setattr(gemm, self._acc_mult_attr(), 1)
344	        s = mSFD.stride
345	        # (N, M, L): N = ((32, 4), rn) column atoms; M = ((vec, 4), rm_k)
346	        # with the vec rows broadcast (stride 0) and 4 consecutive M slots at
347	        # consecutive bytes. M is all-or-nothing per CTA because the host
348	        # allocates rm_k in whole 128-row stripes (multiples of 128/(4*vec)).
349	        layout_nml = cute.make_layout(
350	            (((32, 4), mSFD.shape[1]), ((vec, 4), mSFD.shape[2]), mSFD.shape[0]),
351	            stride=(((16, 4), s[1]), ((0, 1), s[2]), s[0]),
352	        )
353	        sfd_layout = cute.select(layout_nml, [1, 0, 2])  # (M_pad, N_pad, L)
354	        return {self.name: (cute.make_tensor(mSFD.iterator, sfd_layout), norm_const)}
355	
356	    def param_fields(self):
357	        return [(self.name, object, None)]
358	
359	    # --- Cross-warp amax exchange smem (SM120 warp-MMA epilogues only) ---
360	    #
361	    # A 32-wide SF vector can span warp neighbors along its axis: row
362	    # direction when the tiled-MMA warp N run is 16 (interleaved 16-column
363	    # runs; the run is normally widened to 32 instead, see
364	    # GemmSm120.mma_n_warp_run), col direction always (warp M stripes are the
365	    # 16-row mma instruction tiles). The neighbors' partial amaxes meet
366	    # through this buffer: one f32 per (epi-subtile SF slot, member warp),
367	    # double-buffered by subtile parity so one epilogue-barrier per subtile is
368	    # WAR-safe. 16-wide vectors (nvfp4) never allocate. The host-side
369	    # condition intentionally matches the trace-time warp_span > 1 geometry;
370	    # begin() asserts if they ever disagree.
371	
372	    def _xwarp_smem_shape(self, epi_tile, warps):
373	        epi_m = cute.size(cute.shape(epi_tile[0]))
374	        epi_n = cute.size(cute.shape(epi_tile[1]))
375	        if self.direction == "col":
376	            return (max(epi_m // 32, 1), epi_n, warps, 2)
377	        return (epi_m, max(epi_n // 32, 1), warps, 2)
378	
379	    def _xwarp_smem_needed(self, vec_eff, warp_shape_mnk, n_warp_run=16, arch=None):
380	        # vec_eff: the SF vector width in acc elements (sf_vec, doubled for a
381	        # gated aux target). n_warp_run: consecutive N columns per warp in the
382	        # tiled-MMA permutation (GemmSm120.mma_n_warp_run) — a vector no wider
383	        # than the run is warp-local; smem_bytes budgets with the conservative
384	        # default 16 (the run is chosen later), the struct hooks pass the real
385	        # value.
386	        if warp_shape_mnk is None:
387	            return False
388	        if self.direction == "col":
389	            # Slot-machinery col only (SM120 warp MMA: 16-row warp M stripes
390	            # vs the 32-row vector). SM100's dedicated redux path needs no
391	            # smem; its (4,1) epi warp shape is also excluded by
392	            # warp_shape[1] > 1 for the arch-less smem_bytes budgeting, the
393	            # struct hooks pass arch.
394	            return (
395	                not self._col_redux_path(arch)
396	                and warp_shape_mnk[0] > 1
397	                and warp_shape_mnk[1] > 1
398	                and vec_eff > 16
399	            )
400	        return warp_shape_mnk[1] > 1 and vec_eff > n_warp_run
401	
402	    def _xwarp_warps(self, warp_shape_mnk):
403	        return warp_shape_mnk[0] if self.direction == "col" else warp_shape_mnk[1]
404	
405	    def smem_bytes(self, arg_tensor, cta_tile_shape_mnk, epi_tile, warp_shape_mnk=None):
406	        # Budget conservatively for an aux target: gated-ness is unknown here,
407	        # assume the doubled acc-space vector.
408	        vec_eff = sf_vec_size_for(arg_tensor.element_type) * (1 if self.quant_output == "D" else 2)
409	        if not self._xwarp_smem_needed(vec_eff, warp_shape_mnk):
410	            return EpiSmemBytes()
411	        return EpiSmemBytes(
412	            unstaged=math.prod(self._xwarp_smem_shape(epi_tile, self._xwarp_warps(warp_shape_mnk)))
413	            * 4
414	        )
415	
416	    def _xwarp_smem_shape_for(self, gemm):
417	        """The exchange smem shape for this compiled config, or None when the
418	        exchange is not needed — the shared guard of the two smem hooks (the
419	        exact geometry, unlike smem_bytes' conservative budget)."""
420	        vec_acc = getattr(gemm, self._vec_attr())
421	        run = getattr(gemm, "mma_n_warp_run", 16)
422	        warp_shape = gemm.epi_smem_warp_shape_mnk()
423	        if not self._xwarp_smem_needed(vec_acc, warp_shape, run, arch=gemm.arch):
424	            return None
425	        return self._xwarp_smem_shape(gemm.epi_tile, self._xwarp_warps(warp_shape))
426	
427	    def smem_struct_field(self, gemm, params):
428	        shape = self._xwarp_smem_shape_for(gemm)
429	        if shape is None:
430	            return None
431	        return (
432	            f"s_{self.name}_xw",
433	            cute.struct.Align[cute.struct.MemRange[Float32, math.prod(shape)], 16],
434	        )

436	    def get_smem_tensor(self, gemm, params, storage_epi):
437	        shape = self._xwarp_smem_shape_for(gemm)
438	        if shape is None:
439	            return None
440	        return getattr(storage_epi, f"s_{self.name}_xw").get_tensor(cute.make_layout(shape))

442	    @cute.jit
443	    def _sfd_gmem_view(self, gemm, param, ctx, atom_cols):
444	        """Partitioned CTA-tile view of the logical (M_pad, N_pad, L) SF
445	        tensor plus the padded-extent limits — shared by the slot-machinery
446	        ``begin`` and the SM100 col ``_begin_col``. CTA-tiles directly when
447	        the tile covers whole SF atoms along N (``atom_cols``: 4 * vec for
448	        row, 128 transposed-atom columns for col) so a fully in-bounds tile
449	        can flush with one autovec copy; otherwise (a fractional atom, e.g.
450	        tile_n 192 vs 128 columns) shifts the origin (domain_offset only
451	        evaluates the layout, no division) and lets partition_for_epilogue
452	        tile by epi_tile, with per-subtile bounds checks at the stores.
453	        Limits are vs the padded SF extents: M is all-or-nothing per CTA
454	        (tile grid and pad are both 128-quantized; for varlen_m the extent is
455	        this batch's tile-aligned padded region, same convention as input
456	        SFA); N can be partial when tile_N doesn't divide the atom coverage.
457	        """
458	        tile_M, tile_N = ctx.tile_M, ctx.tile_N
459	        if const_expr(ctx.varlen_manager.varlen_m):
460	            # Rank-2 M-padded view; shift to this batch's tile-aligned region
461	            # (cu_seqlens_m[b] // 128 + b tiles), same formula as input SFA.
462	            mSFD_mn = ctx.varlen_manager.offset_batch_SFA(param, ctx.batch_idx)
463	        else:
464	            mSFD_mn = param[None, None, ctx.batch_idx]
465	        if const_expr(tile_N % atom_cols == 0):
466	            gSFD = cute.local_tile(
467	                mSFD_mn, (tile_M, tile_N), (ctx.tile_coord_mnkl[0], ctx.tile_coord_mnkl[1])
468	            )
469	        else:
470	            gSFD = cute.domain_offset(
471	                (ctx.tile_coord_mnkl[0] * tile_M, ctx.tile_coord_mnkl[1] * tile_N), mSFD_mn
472	            )
473	        # (CPY, CPY_M, CPY_N, EPI_M, EPI_N); un-retiled t2r partitions index
474	        # element-wise compatibly with tRS_rD (same TV layout; see VecReduce).
475	        tDgSFD = ctx.partition_for_epilogue_fn(gSFD)
476	        if const_expr(ctx.varlen_manager.varlen_m):
477	            len_m = ctx.varlen_manager.len_m(ctx.batch_idx)
478	            m_extent = (len_m + 127) // 128 * 128
479	        else:
480	            m_extent = cute.size(mSFD_mn, mode=[0])
481	        limit_m = Int32(m_extent - ctx.tile_coord_mnkl[0] * tile_M)
482	        limit_n = Int32(cute.size(mSFD_mn, mode=[1]) - ctx.tile_coord_mnkl[1] * tile_N)
483	        return tDgSFD, limit_m, limit_n
484	
485	    @cute.jit
486	    def begin(self, gemm, param, smem_tensor, ctx):
487	        param, norm_const_arg = param
488	        # Load the norm constant once per tile (immediate or device pointer).
489	        norm_const = None
490	        if const_expr(norm_const_arg is not None):
491	            norm_const = utils.load_scalar_or_pointer(norm_const_arg)
492	        if const_expr(self._col_redux_path(gemm.arch)):
493	            return self._begin_col(gemm, param, ctx, norm_const)
494	        # Slot-machinery path: row direction on both arches, col on SM120.
495	        # ``ax`` is the SF vector's axis (1 = along N, 0 = along M); the
496	        # broadcast layout, lane/warp geometry and exchange slot indexing are
497	        # the same construction with M and N swapped.
498	        ax = const_expr(0 if self.direction == "col" else 1)
499	        vec = getattr(gemm, self._vec_attr())
500	        tile_M, tile_N = ctx.tile_M, ctx.tile_N
501	        tDgSFD, limit_m, limit_n = self._sfd_gmem_view(
502	            gemm, param, ctx, atom_cols=const_expr(128 if ax == 0 else 4 * vec)
503	        )
504	        # Register SF-slot tensor: same partitioning of a broadcast layout whose
505	        # codomain is the per-tile SF slot index, so vec elements alias one slot.
506	        if const_expr(ax == 0):
507	            num_sf_m = tile_M // vec
508	            sf_bcast_layout = cute.make_layout(((vec, num_sf_m), tile_N), stride=((0, 1), num_sf_m))
509	        else:
510	            num_sf_n = tile_N // vec
511	            sf_bcast_layout = cute.make_layout((tile_M, (vec, num_sf_n)), stride=(num_sf_n, (0, 1)))
512	        tDrSFD_layout = ctx.partition_for_epilogue_fn(
513	            cute.make_rmem_tensor(sf_bcast_layout, Float32)
514	        ).layout
515	        tDrSFD = cute.make_rmem_tensor(tDrSFD_layout, getattr(gemm, self._sf_dtype_attr()))
516	        # SF vectors may be split across lanes along their axis (e.g. the
517	        # 16dp256b tmem load of tile_m 64 gives each lane 8-column runs, with
518	        # lanes {l, l+16} sharing every row; SM120 col vectors span the 8-lane
519	        # stride-4 column groups of the mma fragment): each thread then owns
520	        # vec / lanes elements of every vector it touches, and the per-thread
521	        # partial amaxes are combined with butterfly shuffles across the lane
522	        # group. On the SM90-style register epilogue (SM120 warp MMA,
523	        # tiled_copy_t2r is None) the geometry comes from the r2s copy's
524	        # SOURCE TV layout — same tiled_copy selection as VecReduce.
525	        tiled_copy = (
526	            ctx.tiled_copy_t2r if const_expr(ctx.tiled_copy_t2r is not None) else ctx.tiled_copy_r2s
527	        )
528	        lane_layout_MN, warp_layout_MN = _get_lane_warp_layouts(
529	            tiled_copy, reference_src=const_expr(ctx.tiled_copy_t2r is None)
530	        )
531	        lanes_in_ax = cute.size(lane_layout_MN[ax])
532	        warps_in_ax = cute.size(warp_layout_MN[ax])
533	        lane_stride = lane_layout_MN[ax].stride if lanes_in_ax > 1 else 0
534	        # Data-driven containment: elems_per_slot says how much of each SF
535	        # vector this thread holds. Thread-local vectors (elems_per_slot ==
536	        # vec) need no cross-lane work. Otherwise the vector spans `span`
537	        # consecutive lane subgroups, combined by butterfly shuffles (and only
538	        # the subgroup leader stores); if it exceeds the warp's lane group
539	        # (SM120 warp MMA: 16-column warp N runs or 16-row warp M stripes vs
540	        # a 32-wide SF vector), the remainder spans warp_span warp neighbors
541	        # along the axis, combined through the sExch smem buffer.
542	        tDrSFD_sub0 = cute.group_modes(tDrSFD, 3, cute.rank(tDrSFD))[None, None, None, 0]
543	        n_slots_sub = cute.size(cute.filter_zeros(tDrSFD_sub0))
544	        elems_per_slot = cute.size(tDrSFD_sub0) // n_slots_sub
545	        assert cute.size(tDrSFD_sub0) == elems_per_slot * n_slots_sub
546	        assert vec % elems_per_slot == 0, (
547	            f"SFD: thread holds {elems_per_slot} elements per SF slot, not a divisor of "
548	            f"the vector size {vec}; check tile_m / epi tile"
549	        )
550	        span = vec // elems_per_slot
551	        if const_expr(span <= lanes_in_ax):
552	            lane_span = span
553	            warp_span = 1
554	            assert lanes_in_ax % lane_span == 0, (
555	                f"SF vector spans {lane_span} lanes but the lane group is {lanes_in_ax}"
556	            )
557	        else:
558	            assert span % lanes_in_ax == 0 and lanes_in_ax == (1 << int(math.log2(lanes_in_ax)))
559	            lane_span = lanes_in_ax
560	            warp_span = span // lanes_in_ax
561	            assert warp_span <= warps_in_ax and warps_in_ax % warp_span == 0, (
562	                f"SF vector spans {warp_span} warps along its axis but only {warps_in_ax} exist"
563	            )

568	            assert smem_tensor is not None, (
569	                "SFD cross-warp amax exchange needs its smem buffer (smem_struct_field "
570	                "and the trace-time geometry disagree)"

572	            warp_idx = cute.arch.make_warp_uniform(ctx.tidx // cute.arch.WARP_SIZE)

578	        sub_layout = tDrSFD_sub0.layout
579	        tDrAmax = cute.make_rmem_tensor(sub_layout, Float32)
580	        tDrScale = cute.make_rmem_tensor(sub_layout, Float32)
581	        return _SfdRowState(
582	            tDgSFD,
583	            tDrSFD,
584	            tDrAmax,
585	            tDrScale,
586	            limit_m,
587	            limit_n,
588	            lane_span,
589	            lane_stride,
590	            norm_const,
591	            warp_span,
592	            warp_member,
593	            sExch,
594	            tDcD,

718	    @staticmethod
719	    def _sf_pack_width(tDg_flt, max_pack=4):
720	        """Static store width (bytes) for the filtered SF gmem view: the
721	        leading contiguous run after coalescing. 1 when a thread's slots are
722	        not adjacent (e.g. 16dp loads interleave lane halves byte-by-byte)."""
723	        lay = cute.coalesce(tDg_flt).layout
724	        shape, stride = lay.shape, lay.stride
725	        if isinstance(shape, int):
726	            shape, stride = (shape,), (stride,)
727	        if not isinstance(stride[0], int) or stride[0] != 1 or not isinstance(shape[0], int):
728	            return 1
729	        return math.gcd(shape[0], max_pack)

731	    @staticmethod
732	    @cute.jit
733	    def _sf_packed_copy(tDr_flt, tDg_flt, pack):
734	        """Store SF bytes packed as one u32/u16 per `pack` consecutive slots.
735	
736	        autovec_copy alone emits byte stores here: the per-thread gmem offset
737	        (16*(m%32) + 4*(m//32%4) + slot) defeats its alignment analysis, so
738	        widen explicitly — all strides and the base are multiples of `pack`.
739	        """
740	        if const_expr(pack == 4):
741	            wide = Int32
742	        elif const_expr(pack == 2):
743	            wide = cutlass.Int16
744	        else:
745	            wide = None
746	        if const_expr(wide is not None):
747	            # SF slot addresses are pack-aligned by construction (16 B base,
748	            # strides 16/4/1 within an atom, 512 B across atoms), but the
749	            # compiler's alignment analysis can lose that through tile
750	            # divisions (e.g. 64-row tiles) — assert it explicitly.
751	            tDg_flt = cute.coalesce(tDg_flt)
752	            tDg_flt = cute.make_tensor(tDg_flt.iterator.align(pack), tDg_flt.layout)
753	            cute.autovec_copy(
754	                cute.coalesce(cute.recast_tensor(cute.coalesce(tDr_flt), wide)),
755	                cute.coalesce(cute.recast_tensor(tDg_flt, wide)),
756	            )
757	        else:
758	            cute.autovec_copy(tDr_flt, tDg_flt)

760	    @cute.jit
761	    def _flush_per_subtile(self, gemm, tDgSFD, tDrSFD, epi_tile, limit_m, limit_n):
762	        """Per-subtile flush with a uniform bounds check. Every epi subtile
763	        width divides the SF atom coverage along both axes (epi_m divides the
764	        128-row pad, epi tile N divides the 4*vec atom columns), so each
765	        subtile is fully inside or fully outside the padded SF extent."""
766	        epi_m_size = cute.size(epi_tile[0])
767	        epi_n_size = cute.size(epi_tile[1])
768	        cnt_m = gemm.cta_tile_shape_mnk[0] // epi_m_size
769	        cnt_n = gemm.cta_tile_shape_mnk[1] // epi_n_size
770	        tDrSFD_g = cute.group_modes(tDrSFD, 3, cute.rank(tDrSFD))
771	        for em in cutlass.range_constexpr(cnt_m):
772	            for en in cutlass.range_constexpr(cnt_n):
773	                if (em + 1) * epi_m_size <= limit_m and (en + 1) * epi_n_size <= limit_n:
774	                    tDrSFD_cur = tDrSFD_g[None, None, None, (em, en)]
775	                    tDgSFD_cur = cute.filter_zeros(tDgSFD[None, None, None, em, en])
776	                    self._sf_packed_copy(
777	                        cute.filter_zeros(tDrSFD_cur),
778	                        tDgSFD_cur,
779	                        self._sf_pack_width(tDgSFD_cur),
780	                    )

782	    @cute.jit
783	    def end(
784	        self,
785	        gemm,
786	        param,
787	        state,
788	        epi_tile,
789	        tiled_copy_t2r,
790	        tiled_copy_r2s,
791	        tile_coord_mnkl,
792	        varlen_manager,
793	        tidx,
794	    ):
795	        if const_expr(self._col_redux_path(gemm.arch)):
796	            # Column-direction SF bytes are stored inline per subtile in
797	            # sfd_quantize_subtile_col (per-byte designated-lane stores).
798	            return
799	        tDgSFD, tDrSFD = state.tDgSFD, state.tDrSFD
800	        limit_m, limit_n = state.limit_m, state.limit_n
801	        lane_span, lane_stride = state.lane_span, state.lane_stride
802	        vec = getattr(gemm, self._vec_attr())
803	        tile_N = gemm.cta_tile_shape_mnk[1]
804	        # When SF vectors are lane-split, every lane in the subgroup holds
805	        # identical SF bytes; only the subgroup leader stores. Warp-split
806	        # vectors (SM120): every member warp holds identical bytes after the
807	        # sExch fold; only member 0 stores.
808	        is_leader = Boolean(True)
809	        if const_expr(lane_span > 1):
810	            lane = cute.arch.lane_idx()
811	            is_leader = (lane // lane_stride) % lane_span == 0
812	        if const_expr(state.warp_span > 1):
813	            is_leader = is_leader & (state.warp_member == 0)
814	        # Whole-tile autovec flush only when begin() CTA-tiled the gmem view
815	        # (row direction, tile_N covering whole atoms); the col transposed
816	        # atom stores per byte anyway, so per-subtile costs nothing extra.
817	        whole_tile_ok = const_expr(self.direction == "row" and tile_N % (4 * vec) == 0)
818	        if is_leader and limit_m > 0:
819	            if const_expr(whole_tile_ok):
820	                if limit_m >= gemm.cta_tile_shape_mnk[0] and limit_n >= tile_N:
821	                    # Whole tile in bounds: vectorized stores (4 consecutive SF
822	                    # slots of a row are consecutive bytes -> 4-byte stores,
823	                    # when this thread's slots are actually adjacent).
824	                    tDgSFD_flt = cute.filter_zeros(tDgSFD)
825	                    self._sf_packed_copy(
826	                        cute.filter_zeros(tDrSFD), tDgSFD_flt, self._sf_pack_width(tDgSFD_flt)
827	                    )
828	                else:
829	                    self._flush_per_subtile(gemm, tDgSFD, tDrSFD, epi_tile, limit_m, limit_n)
830	            else:
831	                self._flush_per_subtile(gemm, tDgSFD, tDrSFD, epi_tile, limit_m, limit_n)

834	@cute.jit
835	def sfd_quantize_subtile(
836	    gemm,
837	    tDrAmax,
838	    tDrScale,
839	    tDrSFD_cur,
840	    tRS_rD,
841	    lane_span,
842	    lane_stride,
843	    norm_const=None,
844	    value_dtype=None,
845	    acc_stride=1,
846	    xwarp=None,
847	):
848	    """Compute + quantize SF for one subtile and rescale tRS_rD in place.
849	
850	    Called from BlockScaleFactorStore.quantize (the driver's store loop),
851	    after all element-wise epilogue ops, so the scale factors reflect the
852	    final output values.
853	
854	    The SF slot tensors live in accumulator space. ``acc_stride`` maps
855	    fragment element i to acc element acc_stride * i: 1 for full-tile values,
856	    2 for a halved gated postact whose element i is act(acc[2i], acc[2i+1]).
857	
858	    ``xwarp`` (SF vectors spanning warps along their axis, SM120 warp MMA): a
859	    ``(sExch, tDcD_cur, (epi_m, epi_n), (div_m, div_n), warp_member,
860	    warp_span, barrier)`` bundle. After the in-warp butterfly, each warp's
861	    per-slot partial amax is published to sExch[(m % epi_m) // div_m,
862	    (n % epi_n) // div_n, warp_member] — the divisor is the vector width on
863	    the vector's axis and 1 on the other — the barrier syncs the epilogue
864	    warps, and every lane folds in the other members' partials, so the
865	    quantize and rescale below stay lane-local and every warp stores
866	    identical SF bytes (a single member does, see end()).
867	    """
868	    if const_expr(value_dtype is None):
869	        value_dtype = gemm.d_dtype
870	    tDrAmax_flt = cute.filter_zeros(tDrAmax)
871	    tDrScale_flt = cute.filter_zeros(tDrScale)
872	    tDrSFD_flt = cute.filter_zeros(tDrSFD_cur)
873	    tDrAmax_flt.fill(0.0)
874	    # Zero-stride broadcast layout accumulates each element into its SF slot,
875	    # independent of the fragment's register order. Off SM100, the whole fold
876	    # — element accumulate, lane butterfly, cross-warp exchange — runs on
877	    # two-input max.xorsign.abs (fmax abs=True): it preserves the maximum
878	    # MAGNITUDE while XORing operand signs, so no per-element absf is needed
879	    # and the arbitrary accumulated sign is cleared once per slot at the end
880	    # (same pattern as the VecReduce max_abs epilogue). On SM100 the plain
881	    # fmax(acc, |x|) chain is kept: ptxas fuses it into 3-input FMNMX3.ABS
882	    # (abs is an operand modifier there, and FMNMX3 is SM100-only), which
883	    # the two-input xorsign form would defeat.
884	    xorsign = const_expr(gemm.arch != 100)
885	    for i in cutlass.range(cute.size(tRS_rD), unroll_full=True):
886	        if const_expr(xorsign):
887	            tDrAmax[acc_stride * i] = cute.arch.fmax(tDrAmax[acc_stride * i], tRS_rD[i], abs=True)
888	        else:
889	            tDrAmax[acc_stride * i] = cute.arch.fmax(
890	                tDrAmax[acc_stride * i], cute.math.absf(tRS_rD[i])
891	            )
892	    if const_expr(lane_span > 1):
893	        # SF vectors split across lane_span consecutive lane subgroups along
894	        # the vector's axis: butterfly-combine the per-lane partial amaxes;
895	        # every lane ends up with the full-vector amax (with xorsign: the
896	        # magnitude — signs diverge per lane and are cleared below) so the
897	        # rescale below stays lane-local.
898	        for vi in cutlass.range_constexpr(cute.size(tDrAmax_flt)):
899	            v = tDrAmax_flt[vi]
900	            step = lane_span // 2
901	            while step > 0:
902	                v = cute.arch.fmax(
903	                    v, cute.arch.shuffle_sync_bfly(v, offset=step * lane_stride), abs=xorsign
904	                )
905	                step //= 2
906	            tDrAmax_flt[vi] = v
907	    if const_expr(xwarp is not None):
908	        sExch, tDcD_cur, epi_mn, slot_div, warp_member, warp_span, barrier = xwarp
909	        epi_m_size, epi_n_size = epi_mn
910	        div_m, div_n = slot_div
911	        # Publish this warp's per-slot partials (sign-garbled, magnitudes
912	        # correct). Aliased elements (and the lanes of a subgroup) write the
913	        # same value to the same slot — benign. The coord partition lives in
914	        # ACC space, so a halved gated fragment indexes it at acc_stride * i,
915	        # same as the slot tensors.
916	        for i in cutlass.range(cute.size(tRS_rD), unroll_full=True):
917	            c = tDcD_cur[acc_stride * i]
918	            sExch[(c[0] % epi_m_size) // div_m, (c[1] % epi_n_size) // div_n, warp_member] = (
919	                tDrAmax[acc_stride * i]
920	            )
921	        barrier.arrive_and_wait()
922	        # Fold in every member's partial (including our own — idempotent).
923	        for i in cutlass.range(cute.size(tRS_rD), unroll_full=True):
924	            c = tDcD_cur[acc_stride * i]
925	            v = tDrAmax[acc_stride * i]
926	            for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(warp_span):
927	                v = cute.arch.fmax(
928	                    v,
929	                    sExch[(c[0] % epi_m_size) // div_m, (c[1] % epi_n_size) // div_n, j],
930	                    abs=True,
931	                )
932	            tDrAmax[acc_stride * i] = v
933	    if const_expr(xorsign):
934	        # Clear the XOR-accumulated sign once per slot.
935	        for vi in cutlass.range_constexpr(cute.size(tDrAmax_flt)):
936	            tDrAmax_flt[vi] = cute.math.abs(tDrAmax_flt[vi])
937	    # Shared quantize core: SF bytes + rescale factors from the amaxes (see
938	    # quack.blockscaled.quantize_utils for the cuBLAS/CUTLASS semantics contract).
939	    quantize_sf_slots(tDrAmax_flt, tDrSFD_flt, tDrScale_flt, value_dtype, norm_const=norm_const)
940	    for i in cutlass.range(cute.size(tRS_rD), unroll_full=True):
941	        tRS_rD[i] = tRS_rD[i] * tDrScale[acc_stride * i]

945	def sfd_quantize_subtile_col(
946	    gemm, tDgSFD_cur, tDcSFD_cur, vec, limit_m, limit_n, tRS_rD, norm_const=None, value_dtype=None
947	):
948	    """Column-direction variant of sfd_quantize_subtile: one SF byte per
949	    (32/16-row block, column). Each column's amax is one
950	    ``redux.sync.max.abs.NaN.f32`` across the `vec` lanes of the row group
951	    (lane == row within the warp stripe; SM100a, same instruction the CUTLASS
952	    C++ ColStore uses — a 5-round shuffle butterfly otherwise). Every lane
953	    then rescales its own value and a designated lane per group stores the SF
954	    byte. All per-byte stores — the transposed atom puts adjacent columns'
955	    bytes 16 B apart, so there is nothing to pack.
956	
957	    NaN semantics: redux propagates (a NaN anywhere in the vector poisons the
958	    SF byte, matching CUTLASS); the row direction's thread-local FMNMX chain
959	    currently drops NaNs instead.
960	    """
961	    if const_expr(value_dtype is None):
962	        value_dtype = gemm.d_dtype
963	    rcp_dmax = 1.0 / QUANT_DTYPE_MAX[value_dtype]
964	    if const_expr(norm_const is not None):
965	        norm_scaled = norm_const * rcp_dmax
966	    else:
967	        norm_scaled = Float32(rcp_dmax)
968	    sf_dtype = tDgSFD_cur.element_type
969	    is_e8m0 = const_expr(sf_dtype is cutlass.Float8E8M0FNU)
970	    # 1-slot scratch for the exact e8m0 integer reciprocal (254 - exponent
971	    # byte); scalar setitem to dodge the degenerate-view store bug.
972	    tScratchB = cute.make_rmem_tensor(cute.make_layout(1), cutlass.Uint8)
973	    tScratch_sf = cute.recast_tensor(tScratchB, sf_dtype)
974	    tScratch_e8 = cute.recast_tensor(tScratchB, cutlass.Float8E8M0FNU)
975	    lane = cute.arch.lane_idx()
976	    m_ok = limit_m > 0  # all-or-nothing per CTA (128-row stripes)
977	    for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(cute.size(tRS_rD)):
978	        # Amax over the vec-lane row group; every lane gets it. One
979	        # redux.sync.max.abs.NaN on the SM100 family, shuffle butterfly on
980	        # arches without fp32 redux (SM120).
981	        amax = warp_reduce(tRS_rD[i], cute.arch.fmax, threads_in_group=vec, abs=True, nan=True)
982	        tScratch_sf[0] = sf_dtype(amax * norm_scaled)
983	        # One lane per group stores this column's byte; distribute columns
984	        # round-robin over the group so stores go out in parallel.
985	        if m_ok and (lane % vec) == (i % vec) and tDcSFD_cur[i][1] < limit_n:
986	            tDgSFD_cur[i] = tScratch_sf[0]
987	        # Rescale by the reciprocal of the quantized scale.
988	        if const_expr(is_e8m0):
989	            tScratchB[0] = cutlass.Uint8((254 - tScratchB[0]) & 0xFF)
990	            acc_scale = tScratch_e8[0].to(Float32)
991	        else:
992	            acc_scale = cute.arch.rcp_approx(tScratch_sf[0].to(Float32))
993	        if const_expr(norm_const is not None):
994	            acc_scale = acc_scale * norm_const
995	        tRS_rD[i] = tRS_rD[i] * cute.arch.fmin(acc_scale, FLT_MAX)
